treatment: Northern Corn Leaf Blight is a fungal disease (Exserohilum turcicum) characterized by long, elliptical, tan lesions. To manage this, practice crop rotation with non-grass species and use tillage to bury infected debris. If the disease appears before silking and weather is favorable for spread, apply a foliar fungicide. Avoid overhead irrigation during late afternoon or evening to reduce the duration of leaf wetness.

The leaf shows symptoms of Anthracnose, a fungal infection characterized by dark, necrotic spots and edges. To manage this, prune and destroy all affected leaves to reduce the source of infection. Ensure good air circulation around the plant and avoid watering from above (overhead irrigation), as wet foliage promotes fungal growth. Apply a copper-based or systemic fungicide as a preventative and curative measure.

Rice Blast is caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae. It typically manifests as spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with brown borders and gray centers. To treat and prevent its spread: 1. Avoid excessive use of nitrogenous fertilizers, as they can promote fungal growth. 2. Ensure proper water management; do not let fields dry out completely during the susceptible stages. 3. Destroy infected crop residue after harvest to reduce the source of infection for the next season. 4. Apply a systemic fungicide as soon as the first symptoms appear, especially during the seedling stage or before the panicle emerges.
